description.text:
The promos of Japan's LEGEND years, numbered 001/L-P to 079/L-P and released from September 2009 to August 2010. The LEGEND era began with HeartGold Collection and SoulSilver Collection, and with it the promo suffix changed from DPt-P to L-P.

They came from release campaigns and tournaments for each LEGEND expansion, Gym Challenge store tournaments, Challenge Hiroba, free card battles at Pokémon Centers, the Pokémon Daisuki Club's member ranks, the Legendary Pokémon and Shiny Pokémon Present Campaigns, Domino's Pizza, the LEGEND Perfect Set and the tournament that chose Japan's World Championships players. This set also holds cards marked L-P without a number: the Tropical Tidal Wave of the 2010 World Championships and the Illusion's Zorua and Illusion's Zoroark cards of the 2010 Pokémon Card Design Contest.

description.text:
Given to players at Pokémon Challenge Hiroba (ポケモンチャレンジひろば) events in September 2009, a month before the first expansions of the new Pokémon Card Game LEGEND series, HeartGold Collection and SoulSilver Collection, came out on 9 October 2009. Challenge Hiroba were events at shopping centers where staff taught the game to beginners and ran Card Get Battles. Its text box carries a banner for Pokémon Card Game LEGEND SoulSilver Collection, as does Typhlosion 003/L-P from Pokémon Fan, while Feraligatr 002/L-P from that month's Gym Challenge events carries one for HeartGold Collection.

It was also handed out at Pokémon Day in Roppongi Hills, held at the Roppongi Hills Arena in Tokyo on 26 and 27 September 2009 to celebrate the Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver games, to everyone who joined a corner showing the coming LEGEND cards on a big screen. That month an official notice of 25 September 2009 apologized that three Card Get Battles, on 20 September at Ito-Yokado Ario Yao and Apita Niigata Nishi and on 22 September at Ito-Yokado Koshien, had handed out the wrong participation prize, and offered the right one.

Shin Nagasawa drew it.

description.text:
One of six original holo cards of the launch campaign for HeartGold Collection and SoulSilver Collection, the first expansions of the new Pokémon Card Game LEGEND series, released on 9 October 2009. From that day, while stocks lasted, every two packs of either expansion bought at once came with one of the six, Chikorita, Cyndaquil, Totodile, Mareep, Phanpy and Teddiursa, at random and packed in a small bag. Card shops, Pokémon Centers and convenience stores, except some, took part, and the card came only from the shop where the packs were bought. Each has its own illustration and attacks, the logos of both expansions across the picture, and the words 発売記念カード (launch commemoration card).

Ken Sugimori drew all six.

description.text:
One of eight holo basic Energy cards given to players at Gym Challenge (ジム☆チャレンジ) events at shops of the official Pokémon Card Gym network from September 2009, in place of the DPt-P Energies numbered 022 to 029 that the gyms had given earlier in 2009. The official pages name a holo Energy as the participation prize of the gyms' normal tournaments in November 2009 and in February, April and August 2010, one of the eight at random.

It also came, together with each tournament's own participation card, at the gyms' launch tournaments of the LEGEND expansions: with Sentret 022/L-P for HeartGold Collection and SoulSilver Collection in October 2009, with Scyther 049/L-P or Houndour 050/L-P for Reviving Legends in February 2010, with Zangoose 056/L-P for Lost Link in April 2010 and with Electabuzz 069/L-P for Clash at the Summit in July 2010.

description.text:
The Gold Rank prize of the Pokémon Daisuki Club's PCG Action Points (PCGアクションポイント), which members collected by taking their club card to official events such as Gym Challenge and Challenge Hiroba. Reaching 1,200 points brought this Pikachu by post, packed with a holo Lightning Energy, 014/L-P; it replaced the rank's earlier prize, Pikachu 016/DPt-P. The higher ranks brought Cresselia 020/L-P and Darkrai 021/L-P (Super Rank, 3,200 points), Raichu 044/L-P (Hyper Rank, 5,200), Espeon 053/L-P and Umbreon 054/L-P (Special Rank, 7,200) and Master's Scroll 055/L-P (Master Rank, 8,600).

The club card's service ended on 31 August 2010. Points earned until then still counted, and members who had reached Silver Rank or higher were sent the prize of the rank above their own by 15 October 2010.

Kanako Eo drew it.

Given to everyone who took part in the Knockout Battle of Pokémon Battle Challenge. description.text:
The Hyper Rank prize of the Pokémon Daisuki Club's PCG Action Points (PCGアクションポイント), which members collected by taking their club card to official events such as Gym Challenge and Challenge Hiroba. The rank was added in 2009, and reaching 5,200 points brought this Raichu by post, packed with a holo Lightning Energy, 014/L-P. Above it came Espeon 053/L-P and Umbreon 054/L-P (Special Rank, 7,200 points) and Master's Scroll 055/L-P (Master Rank, 8,600). The ranks below brought Pikachu 019/L-P (Gold Rank, 1,200 points) and Cresselia 020/L-P and Darkrai 021/L-P (Super Rank, 3,200). The club card's service ended on 31 August 2010. Points earned until then still counted, and members who had reached Silver Rank or higher were sent the prize of the rank above their own by 15 October 2010.

It is a Pokémon Prime whose Poké-Power ボルテージアップ moves Lightning Energy from the player's other Pokémon to it as often as they like. Takashi Yamaguchi drew it.

description.text:
Given to every player of the prefectural tournaments of the Pokémon World Championships 2010 Japan Representative Tournament, held in all 47 prefectures of Japan from January 2010. The Pokémon World Championships 2010 Japan Representative Tournament (ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス2010 日本代表決定大会) chose Japan's players for that year's World Championships, for the card game and the video games together, and took Ho-Oh and Lugia as its theme for the HeartGold and SoulSilver games. Players, all members of the Pokémon Daisuki Club, were chosen by lottery; each got Lugia and Ho-Oh, card game players a double-sided Ho-Oh and Lugia playmat as well, and those who brought HeartGold or SoulSilver a shiny Eevee for the game. Players of the two Last Challenge qualifiers of May and June 2010 got neither card.

The qualifiers went on to the final on 20 June 2010 at Tokyo Dome City Prism Hall, whose top finishers got Master's Key 068/L-P and an invitation to the World Championships, held from 13 to 15 August 2010 at the Hilton Waikoloa Village in Hawaii. Takashi Yamaguchi drew both cards.

From that day Gym Challenge (ジム☆チャレンジ) shops of the official Pokémon Card Gym network held launch tournaments in two leagues, one for elementary school children and younger and an open one, where every player got Houndour 050/L-P or Scyther 049/L-P, one at random, with a holo basic Energy, and the top three got Burned Tower 052/L-P with original card goods and a gold Jirachi coin. Challenge Hiroba (ポケモンチャレンジひろば) events held launch battles too, where every player got Scyther or Houndour and the excellence prize was Legend Box 051/L-P.

It carries the Pokémon Card Game LEGEND and Reviving Legends logos on its picture. Scyther can, on heads, take no damage from attacks in the next turn. Its credit reads Illus. Wataru Kawahara / Direc. Shinji Higuchi.

description.text:

description.text:
The trophy card of the final of the Pokémon World Championships 2010 Japan Representative Tournament, held on 20 June 2010 at Tokyo Dome City Prism Hall in Tokyo after prefectural tournaments in all 47 prefectures and two Last Challenge qualifiers. The Pokémon World Championships 2010 Japan Representative Tournament (ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス2010 日本代表決定大会) chose Japan's players for that year's World Championships, for the card game and the video games together, and took Ho-Oh and Lugia as its theme for the HeartGold and SoulSilver games. The top finishers of both games got the card set in an acrylic plaque showing their placing, red for the card game and blue for the video game: 36 cards in all, 20 to card game players and 16 to video game players, with invitations to the World Championships, held from 13 to 15 August 2010 at the Hilton Waikoloa Village in Hawaii.

The card reads ポケモンワールドチャンピオンシップス2010 日本代表決定大会入賞カード, a placing card of the tournament. Master's Key draws a card and, on heads, shuffles itself back into the deck. Yuri Umemura drew it.

sources.title: Pokumon: Illusion’s Zorua (Pokemon Card Design Contest 2010) (L-P)

description.text:
Given, with Illusion's Zoroark, to all 660 prize winners of the Shogakukan Ten Magazines Pokémon Card Game Design Contest (小学館10誌連合 ポケモンカードゲーム デザインコンテスト) of 2010. Ten Shogakukan magazines, Pokémon Fan, Yōchien (幼稚園), Televi-kun, Shōgaku Ichinensei, Ninensei, Sannensei and Yonensei, CoroCoro Comic, Pucchigumi and CoroCoro Ichiban!, asked children to draw Zorua and Zoroark, the new Pokémon of that summer's film, Zoroark: Master of Illusions, which opened in Japan on 10 July 2010; entries closed by 24 April 2010, and the results appeared in the magazines' issues of July 2010 and on the film's site. The judges included Tsunekazu Ishihara and the film's director, Kunihiko Yuyama. Each magazine chose one grand prize winner, whose work was shown with their name at the start of the film and made into a card for them as a set of 100 copies; 50 excellence, 100 special and 500 lucky prizes made up the rest.

This card and its partner, credited to 2010 Pikachu Project, carry the film's logo.

Wikipedia: Pokémon World Championships

description.text:
A gift to the players of the 2010 Pokémon World Championships, held from 13 to 15 August 2010 at the Hilton Waikoloa Village in Hawaii. The card was printed in several languages; this is the Japanese print, with the L-P mark. It is a Goods card with WORLDS 10 on its picture of Pikachu riding a surfboard, and it discards all Goods and Stadiums on the opponent's side on heads, or on the player's own side on tails.

Sumiyoshi Kizuki drew it.
